answerCheck.reason: A depicts a sphere, which occupies three-dimensional space. B, C and D depict a circle, triangle and trapezoid, respectively, all plane figures.
The axis leg becomes the height, the other leg sweeps a circular base, and the hypotenuse sweeps the conical lateral surface. The resulting solid is a cone.
A cone has one circular base. The ellipse in the perspective drawing represents that circle.

answerCheck.derivedAnswer: A. Rotating a right triangle about a leg forms a cone
answerCheck.reason: In A, a triangular region sweeps out a three-dimensional cone. B illustrates a moving line segment generating a surface, while C and D illustrate moving points tracing lines.
The cube in D has square front, left, and top views. The cylinder and cone have circular top views, and the sphere has circular views in all three directions.

answerCheck.derivedAnswer: B: Isosceles triangle, isosceles triangle, circle with its center marked
answerCheck.reason: Both horizontal viewing directions give isosceles triangular profiles. From above, the base projects to a circle and the apex projects to its center.

answerCheck.derivedAnswer: D: Rotating a rectangle through one full revolution about one of its sides
answerCheck.reason: At each height along the axis side, the rectangle sweeps a disk whose radius equals the other side's length. These equal-radius disks form a cylinder. The rotations in A and B instead form a cone and a sphere.
The figure and statement specify one cylinder and one cone, giving 1 + 1 = 2 basic solids.
